rows.fee: Free of charge (single-entry Working Holiday visa; Consulate-General of Japan in Toronto / Vancouver).

rows.work_restrictions: Primary purpose must be holiday, not mainly work or study. Work at bars, cabarets, nightclubs, and other premises affecting public morals is prohibited.

rows.work_restrictions: Primary purpose must be holiday. Incidental work to supplement travel and living expenses is allowed.

rows.funds_required: At least €2,000 with outbound and return tickets; at least €3,200 with only an outbound ticket or with no ticket plus the cost of a one-way fare (Embassy of Japan in Germany).
rows.work_restrictions: Main purpose must be holidays, with optional temporary part-time work. Not for a mainly long-term language-school stay or long-term internship.
rows.second_stay: Yes. Applicants may not have previously travelled, or may have travelled only once, on a Japan Working Holiday visa.
rows.notes: Age 18 to before 31st birthday and funds figures from the Embassy of Japan in Germany. Quota “no limit” from MOFA. Fee: TODO verify.

rows.work_restrictions: US applicants must be bona fide post-secondary students or recent graduates (within one year of graduation), with evidence from the institution. Dependents cannot accompany. rows.second_stay: One-time visa. US nationals may seek an extension of up to 6 months (Working Holiday Info Center).
rows.notes: Age 18–30, 18-month stay, USD 45 fee, and student/recent-graduate rule from the Seattle consulate H-1 page.
